entities.name: Giovanni Michiel
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Giovanni Michiel was an Italian Roman Catholic cardinal and bishop who played a pivotal role in the Council of Trent (1545-1563), a landmark event that shaped the Counter-Reformation and the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation. As a key figure in the council, Michiel contributed significantly to the development of the Tridentine Mass and the establishment of the Jesuit Order. His legacy continued through his involvement in various charitable initiatives and educational institutions during his tenure as bishop of Venice (1503-1521). The consequences of Michiel's actions can still be seen in the enduring influence of the Jesuit Order on Catholic education and social reform.

Michiel was born in 1450s, but exact dates are unknown. He died on August 24, 1503, at the age of approximately 53. His life and legacy have been documented by historians such as Carlo Ginzburg, who has extensively researched Michiel's role in the Council of Trent.

Michiel's contributions to the Tridentine Mass and the Jesuit Order are widely recognized. He was a strong supporter of the Counter-Reformation and played a key role in shaping Catholic doctrine during this period. His legacy continues to influence Catholic education and social reform to this day.
